full_judgment:
Md. Gholam Rabbani J: This Rule arises out of a suit for restitution of conjugal rights by the husband Abdul Mabud Chowdhury against the wife Mosammad Nur Akhtar. Trial Court decreed the suit and on appeal by the wife the decree was affirmed. Hence the Rule obtained by the wife. 

 5. So we are now to consider as to whether in view of the findings of the courts below that the wife has been refusing to perform her marital obligations without excuse, the husband is entitled to get a decree for restitution of conjugal rights. The answer is in favour of the husband on the face of the decisions of the Courts of our sub-continent till to-day. But we are unable to subscribe to them. 

 10. Quran dictates that the Muslims should obey Allah and His Prophet (Sm), From the Hadith quoted above it is found that the Prophet (Sm) did not decree restitution of conjugal rights to Mughith against Baria because she did not wish to live with her husband. Barira's statement, "I am not in need of him." means performance of material obligations on her part is injurious to her life. Further, this Hadith teaches us that the free wish of the wife is the final say in this respect. 

 11. In a case reported in AIR 1922 All 363, the plaintiff Mirza Mumtaz contracted a secret marriage with Nafisunnesa of their own choice and of their free will and when his wife's relatives opposed his access to the wife he sued for restitution of conjugal rights. The suit was decreed by the trial Court and affirmed by the lower appellate Court on the finding, "these two young people married one another of their own choice and of their own will and that the bride's relatives restrained her against her will from going to her husband." Relatives went to the High Court in second appeal which was dismissed. 

 13. We, therefore, do not find any cause in the instant suit for granting the decree for restitution of conjugal rights. But she is not entitled to get the deferred dower or maintenance. 

 14. The result is that this Rule is made absolute without cost. Judgment and decree dated 29-4-95 of the Court of Subordinate Judge and 2nd Commercial Court, Chittagong, in PC Appeal No. 9 of 1994 as well as those dated 31-1-94 of the 1st Court Assistant Judge and Family Court, Patiya, Chittagong, in Family Suit No. 56 of 1992 are set aside and the suit is dismissed without costs with the effect that the defendant No.1 Musammat Nur Akhtar shall get neither the deferred dower nor maintenance for herself during the subsisting of the marriage.
